title: Dispatch CUS 2: Doorway Appears in the Wall of a Bookbinder’s Shop
summary: A resident of the missing street asks why strangers are looking through her hall.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A narrow door appeared yesterday between the shelves at Samuel Keene’s bookshop. It opens onto the hall of a house marked 8 Vesper Row. A woman who identified herself as Ada Keene asked Mr. Keene to close it, saying that people had been peering into her home since morning.

Mr. Keene recognized her. She recognized him only after he gave his name. In the house beyond the door, she says her husband Samuel died nine years ago, and she has since lived with their daughter. In the bookshop, Mr. Keene has no daughter. Neither claims that the other is an impostor.

Dr. Lenora Saye of the Eidetical Institute inspected the threshold. From the street, the bookshop wall is continuous brick. From within, the new door has hinges and a worn handle. The rooms beyond remain visible while someone holds it open, though their dimensions exceed the space occupied by the shop and the neighboring bakery.

Miss Morrow compared the census entry for 8 Vesper Row with Ada Keene’s account. It correctly names her daughter, her husband’s death, and the number of upstairs rooms. Mrs. Keene has a census receipt signed by an enumerator whose name does not appear on Alderwick’s staff list.

The council has asked visitors to stay away from North Loom Street while the doorway is examined. Mr. Keene has agreed not to board it up. “There is a person on the other side,” he told our reporter. “I knew that much before I knew who she was.”
